purpose: Test whether RECE's existing preservation mechanism (retain_texts) prevents historical-prompt corruption when applied AT Stage 1, before the damage occurs -- not just at Stage-2 refinement, after it. Existing-method control, not a new method.

parent.note: untouched author parent, same as S1's parent; NEVER build from S1_Stage1 or any refined checkpoint

comparator: existing S1_Stage1 (blank preservation) -- images, labels, predictions reused unmodified, not regenerated

reused_panel.design: 20 cases each: golf ball, English springer, French horn, parachute -- identical manifest, not reconstructed or rewritten

execution_order: 1. Verify parent hash, manifest hash, pinned-source checks.
2. Build S1_STAGE1_HISTORY from the untouched parent (GPU, native fp32 Stage-1 edit only).
3. Verify exactly 32 changed keys, 654 unchanged, all finite, exact reload.
4. Generate 80 images on the reused manifest; release GPU.
5. Individually review all 40 target-role images (golf ball, French horn) at native 512px; grid-review the 2 retained classes (parachute, English springer), escalating on uncertainty.
6. Freeze and hash labels before classification.
8. Compute joint outcomes against S1_Stage1, GolfBall_parent, and M0.
tolerances: native fp32 Stage-1 verification only (exact key-set/reload checks); the fp64 reference solver's 1e-10 backward-error tolerance does NOT apply here and is not imposed
scoped_stop_rule: on a consequential provenance or source-drift failure, stop and preserve evidence; narrow runtime fixes that leave scientific settings unchanged are allowed
forbidden: automatic advance to refinement even if Stage 1 improves
